title: Impact of Rent Control Expansion on Urban Rental Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

The data structure is a classic DID setup with:
- `treated`: binary indicator for districts subject to rent control expansion
- `post`: binary indicator for the post-policy period
- `treat_x_post`: the interaction term (DID estimator)
- `y`: log rental prices (outcome)

The DID estimator compares the change in log rental prices before and after the policy expansion between treated districts (those receiving rent control) and untreated districts (control group).

**Key Assumption: Parallel Trends** — In the absence of the rent control expansion, treated and untreated districts would have followed the same trend in log rental prices. This is plausible if the treatment assignment was not driven by differential pre-existing trends in rental prices. We will verify this by examining pre-treatment means and testing for baseline differences. With only two periods, a formal pre-trends test is limited, but we can check balance.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# DID Analysis: Impact of Rent Control Expansion on Rental Prices
# ============================================================

library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s38_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "rows,", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("\nSummary statistics:\n")
summary(df)

# Check group sizes
cat("\n=== Group Structure ===\n")
print(table(Treated = df$treated, Post = df$post))

# Group means
cat("\n=== Group Means (Log Rental Prices) ===\n")
group_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(group_means)

# Manual DID calculation
mean_treated_pre  <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
mean_treated_post <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])
mean_control_pre  <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])
mean_control_post <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])

did_manual <- (mean_treated_post - mean_treated_pre) - (mean_control_post - mean_control_pre)
cat("\n=== Manual DID Calculation ===\n")
cat("Treated Pre: ", round(mean_treated_pre, 4), "\n")
cat("Treated Post:", round(mean_treated_post, 4), "\n")
cat("Control Pre: ", round(mean_control_pre, 4), "\n")
cat("Control Post:", round(mean_control_post, 4), "\n")
cat("DID Estimate: ", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")

# ============================================================
# Primary DID Regression
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== PRIMARY DID REGRESSION ===\n")
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(did_model)

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== DID with Robust Standard Errors (HC1) ===\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# ============================================================
# Key Result
# ============================================================
coef_did <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
se_did <- sqrt(vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1")["treat_x_post", "treat_x_post"])
ci_lower <- coef_did - 1.96 * se_did
ci_upper <- coef_did + 1.96 * se_did

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("  MAIN RESULT: DID ESTIMATE\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coefficient (treat_x_post): %.4f\n", coef_did))
cat(sprintf("  Robust SE:                  %.4f\n", se_did))
cat(sprintf("  t-statistic:                %.4f\n", coef_did / se_did))
cat(sprintf("  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci_lower, ci_upper))
cat("========================================\n")

# ============================================================
# Robustness Check 1: Unit fixed effects
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Unit Fixed Effects ===\n")
did_fe <- lm(y ~ factor(unit_id) + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
cat(sprintf("DID with unit FE: %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n",
            coef(did_fe)["treat_x_post"],
            summary(did_fe)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]))

# ============================================================
# Robustness Check 2: Pre-treatment balance test
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Pre-Treatment Balance ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
balance_test <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_data)
cat(sprintf("Pre-treatment mean (Control): %.4f\n", balance_test$estimate[1]))
cat(sprintf("Pre-treatment mean (Treated): %.4f\n", balance_test$estimate[2]))
cat(sprintf("Difference p-value: %.4f\n", balance_test$p.value))
if (balance_test$p.value > 0.05) {
  cat("-> No significant pre-treatment difference (supports parallel trends)\n")
} else {
  cat("-> WARNING: Significant pre-treatment difference detected\n")
}

# ============================================================
# Robustness Check 3: Placebo test (effect in pre-period should be zero)
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Median Regression (Quantile) ===\n")
if (requireNamespace("quantreg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(quantreg)
  qr_model <- rq(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df, tau = 0.5)
  cat(sprintf("Median regression DID estimate: %.4f\n", coef(qr_model)["treat_x_post"]))
} else {
  cat("quantreg package not available; skipping.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Negative.** Rent control policies are designed to suppress rental prices. The DID coefficient on `treat_x_post` should be **negative**, indicating that districts experiencing rent control expansion saw a relative decline (or smaller increase) in log rental prices compared to control districts.

**Expected magnitude:** Typical rent control effects in the empirical literature range from **-0.05 to -0.30 log points** (roughly 5–25% reduction in rental prices), depending on the stringency of the policy and the time horizon. Given this is a simulated dataset with a clear DID structure, I expect a statistically significant negative coefficient, likely in the range of **-0.10 to -0.50 log points**.

**Interpretation:** A coefficient of, say, -0.20 would imply that rent control expansion reduced rental prices by approximately 20% in treated districts relative to the counterfactual trend observed in control districts. The robustness checks (unit fixed effects, robust standard errors, balance tests) should confirm the stability of this estimate.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log rental prices over time between treated and untreated districts.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of rent control policies led to a decrease in log rental prices in treated districts.
